I've constructed a countably infinite magma satisfying Equation 5093 while refuting Equation 2 (x = y), formalized
end-to-end in Lean 4 against the pinned official ETP Magma, Equation5093, and Equation2 interfaces. Combined with
ETP's existing finite-triviality theorem, this resolves the open question stated in the pinned blueprint at ETP
commit 7e276a2d05e84e3eef02432abfd0718e78f7abfa: Equation 5093 is an Austin law.

Disclosure: I'm not a mathematician by training, and this work was largely AI-driven under my direction. Multiple
OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude agents contributed to the mathematical exploration, Lean implementation and
repair, skeptical review, and packaging. The workflow shifted from ad hoc parallel agents to a roughly ten-agent
hierarchy with explicit claim ownership.

The operational history, role structure, and frozen hashes are recorded in RESET_HANDOFF.md. For the E5093 result,
I am relying on Lean's kernel checking rather than claiming mathematical authority of my own. I reproduced the
build and checked the frozen hashes. The human-readable results discussed below have received extensive AI review
but no expert human review, and I would especially welcome scrutiny of them.

The construction, in short: $\delta$ is a total injective self-map of a countably generated free group satisfying a
functional “grid law.” Defining

$$
u \mathbin{\diamond} v = v\delta(u^{-1}v)
$$

then makes the resulting magma satisfy Equation 5093. The map $\delta$ is constructed as the limit of finite
injective partial maps using greedy free-product extensions and an invariant preventing collisions.

A fuller derivation, together with a proposed family generalization involving a threshold family $H_n$ and its dual
$K_n$, appears in theorem.md. Only the E5093 case is presently Lean-verified; the dual and general family remain
human-readable arguments.

- The final theorem is:

exists_countable_infinite_etp_model :
∃ (G : Type) (_ : Magma G) (_ : Countable G) (_ : Infinite G),
Equation5093 G ∧ ¬ Equation2 G

- Each of the five exported declarations has measured axiom closure exactly [propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound].

- The source contains no sorry, admit, custom axioms, unsafe, or native_decide.
- A normalized release packet in ETP's ManuallyProved layout builds successfully against the pinned checkout.
- The release exports the theorem Equation5093_not_implies_Equation2 with the @[equational_result] attribute.
- The official extraction pipeline recovered both the infinite E5093 fact and the E5093-to-E2 nonimplication.
- A complete clean source-semantic replay finished with SOURCE_SEMANTIC_REPLAY_PASS.

I am not making a literature-wide novelty or priority claim. A bounded check of the pinned ETP sources found no
previous resolution there, but I have not performed a broader literature search. The finite-collapse theorem and
general free-group tools are prior work. There is no upstream PR, merge, current-main rebase, or maintainer
acceptance yet.

I would appreciate guidance on whether anyone is already working on E5093, where a construction of this size should
live in ETP, whether the module structure should be reduced before a PR, and whether the blueprint should be
updated in the same contribution.
